title: Fifty Years of the Portuguese Minimum Wage: Real Erosion, the Productivity Gap, and the Limits of Regional Identification

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: School of Media Arts and Design, Polytechnic of Porto, Portugal

description:
Reproducible study of Portugal's statutory minimum wage from its introduction in May 1974 to 2026, assembled from primary law.

The statutory series is read from the acts themselves, retrieved from the Diário da República by permanent identifier, and includes the regional schedules of Madeira and the Azores. It is combined with a consumer price index and a productivity series reaching back to the 1960s to document the long-run record: the real wage floor fell through the inflation of the late 1970s and early 1980s and did not regain its 1974 level for four decades, while output per worker more than doubled.

The study also documents why the regional variation available in Portugal cannot identify the price pass-through of minimum-wage policy: the Azorean supplement is proportional and contributes no independent timing, Madeira is the only region legislating its own value, and with the small number of Portuguese regions conventional cluster-robust inference rejects a true null far above its nominal size.
